resolution.finding: F01 (major): unresolved hard gates described as passed or already deferrable until release
resolution.note: ADR §§3.2, 7 and 9 now state five scoped passes and two uncertain hard gates, make the scores/recommendation provisional, and explicitly leave the sequencing exception to Q-D. This matches plan.md:117-125. No owner decision is presumed.

resolution.finding: F02 (major): Windows windows-sys FFI described as safe wrappers
resolution.note: ADR §2.4, §7.1 and §9 now distinguish safe higher-level macOS/Linux wrappers from typed but unsafe Windows FFI, record the 20 unsafe sites, and preserve Go typed x/sys DPAPI. X4 windows RESULTS.md:37-40,66,76-89 supports these distinctions; DPAPI/CNG/TPM execution remains unclaimed.

resolution.finding: F03 (major): demonstrated batch-path injection understated beside unqualified correct escaping
resolution.note: ADR §2.4, security gate, §3.1 and §7.1 now explicitly identify command injection and wrong-file execution through argv[0]; §9 limits correct escaping to arguments and refers to §9.7. The M01 path refusal remains mandatory. This matches m00-wf8/x1b-review-rust.json:70,97 and g02-rust-x1b-windows.json:727. The separate new threat-model error is N01 below; the original impact/escaping omission is corrected.

resolution.finding: F04 (major): most Go cells overstated the calibrated X2 count
resolution.note: ADR §7.1 now states 5/12 Go cells, T1 3/3 and T3 2/3, versus 0/12 Rust; §9 narrows 5/6 to the implementers of those two tasks and preserves two correlated causes, the small sample, and inherited Rust baseline recovery. X2 RESULTS.md:192-225,251-267,280-297 supports the count.

resolution.finding: F05 (major): incompatible Iroh-in-V1 and midpoint explanations for the 4/4 release row
resolution.note: ADR §7.1 explicitly selects Iroh in V1 as the primary scenario and calls 4/4 an offsetting judgment: Go release advantages offset the additional Rust helper/toolchain. The conflicting midpoint and explicit in-V1 3/4 score are removed. This is the first resolution allowed by the original finding and is consistent with orchestrator-prereg.md. Recomputed 3.50/3.90 and deferred 3.70/3.65 are correct. N02 is a separate remaining qualitative helper-scenario inconsistency.

resolution.finding: F06 (major): unlike static/dynamic PIE variants compared without their linkage tradeoff
resolution.note: ADR §2.4 and §7.1 now say both defaults are static non-PIE, Go obtained PIE/full RELRO as a dynamic build requiring a glibc interpreter, and Rust static-musl PIE was not achieved with the stable flags tried. §9 also limits the negative conclusion to tried flags. This matches X3 RESULTS.md:169-199.

resolution.finding: F07 (minor): stale prototype commits and native linux-x64 coverage scope
resolution.note: ADR §2.1 labels 38b6b72/d8f0cbe as round-3 candidates and separately names post-X1b 84c7665/001a791; §2.3 labels the emulation statement as round-3 history; §7.1 explicitly separates native x64 baseline execution from post-fix Windows and arm64 checks. Both X1b records confirm no fresh linux-x64 execution.

resolution.finding: F08 (minor): 18 Go modules incorrectly described as entirely MIT/BSD
resolution.note: ADR licensing row now says 17 third-party modules, all MIT/BSD-3, and explicitly excludes the unlicensed main module from the successful check. X3 RESULTS.md:78,93 and its license-check result support this.

resolution.finding: F09 (minor): X2 rubric sensitivity cited D3(k) instead of D3(l)
resolution.note: ADR §7.3:508 now cites D3(l), which is the X2 rubric at §10:690-696; D3(k) remains the Windows batch-path ruling.

resolution.finding: F10 (minor): unresolved G03 rows all called blocked and second Linux account omitted
resolution.note: ADR §3.1 and Q-C now distinguish blocked rows from in-progress/inconclusive rows and include a second Linux account with sudo. docs/research/g03-windows-wsl.md:19-28 confirms Mode A elevation and Mode B endpoint permissions are in_progress/inconclusive; Windows and Linux second-account requirements remain distinct.

new_findings.claim: The new threat-model rationale says exploiting the script path needs control of both a directory name and an environment variable.
new_findings.evidence: The retained wrong-file probe uses the already-existing OS variable, not an attacker-supplied OS value: Probe-X1bRust.ps1:338-357 constructs os%OS%y and os + $env:OS + y, and the launch overrides only ARGVDUMP_OUT. batch2.scriptpath_existing_var_runs_other_file ran the other batch file, as recorded in m00-wf8/x1b-review-rust.json:70 and g02-rust-x1b-windows.json:727. The bespoke-variable command-injection probe does control HMRDIRVAR, but that is one demonstrated attack configuration, not a necessary condition for every path exploit.
new_findings.fix: Narrow the claim to the demonstrated HMRDIRVAR command-injection probe. Explicitly state that wrong-file execution also occurred with an existing variable whose value the attacker need not control, provided the expanded destination can be populated. Present the lower likelihood of attacker-influenced configured paths as the orchestrator threat-model judgment, rather than a universal technical prerequisite. Preserve the recorded non-gating ruling and M01 refusal obligation; this finding does not change the 71/71 verdict.

new_findings.claim: If Iroh is a supervised helper even in Rust, the release row would still lean Rust, by less.
new_findings.evidence: The corrected primary release row at §7.1:455 is explicitly 4/4 with Iroh in V1, an offsetting judgment; it does not currently lean Rust. X5 supports two artifacts but one language/toolchain for the Rust-helper option, not a scored Rust-leading release row. No alternative helper-specific numeric row is supplied.
new_findings.fix: Say the one-language/toolchain advantage remains but the artifact-count advantage disappears, and identify the overall comparison as a judgment. If asserting a release-row lean, give its explicit scenario scores and recompute totals; do not describe the primary 4/4 row as already Rust-leading.

new_findings.claim: The text says at least one Go implementer avoided each pitfall and says all were fixable or avoidable as one implementer in each X2 task showed; the T1 summary also says on Linux nothing recovers it.
new_findings.evidence: All three Go T1 cells still have a calibrated P1 major (X2 RESULTS.md:192-210). go-opus1 only partly avoided the recovery trap by handling SIGCONT while running (X2 RESULTS.md:219-225,288-294). The independent re-run confirms kill -CONT %1 finishes go-opus1 on Linux as well as macOS (t1-calibration/verify/README.md:125-133), although the keyboard/fg ladder fails on Linux (103-117). Full avoidance was demonstrated by go-opus2 in T3, not by any T1 cell. ADR §6.2:415 correctly says partly, but these summaries drop that qualification.
new_findings.fix: Use avoided or partly avoided, and distinguish T1 partial SIGCONT handling plus proposed standard-library fixes from T3 demonstrated full repaint. Limit the Linux nothing-recovers statement to the tested fg/terminal-key ladder. Keep the existing 3/3 T1 major count and rubric unchanged.

new_findings.claim: Go's bytes change only with its toolchain version.
new_findings.evidence: The retained X1b/X2 rebuild mismatches are explained by Go 1.27.1 versus 1.27.2, but X3 RESULTS.md:121-124 also conditions darwin cross-host equality on the same ad-hoc signing and filename, and uses a specific recipe and tested hosts. The evidence does not establish that toolchain version is the only possible input affecting Go artifact bytes.
new_findings.fix: State that the observed Go round-4 rebuild drift was explained by the toolchain patch upgrade, while Rust's observed drift was not diagnosed. Avoid the categorical only claim.

summary: All 10 original fidelity findings resolved (6 major, 4 minor). No arithmetic error: orchestrator 3.50/3.90, Codex 3.75/3.80, Fable 3.70/3.90, Opus 3.50/4.00; every numeric §7 sensitivity example recomputes correctly. One new major overstates the prerequisites of batch-path exploitation in the revised §9.7/D3(k) threat-model rationale; three minor wording issues concern the helper-scenario row, partial T1 avoidance/recovery, and the Go reproducibility only claim. No blocker and no new native execution performed. The recommendation direction is not re-selected by this review.
